notes: Crisp now fixes combed footage itself. Old tapes, DVD rips and broadcast recordings store each frame as two half-pictures taken a moment apart, which shows up as fine horizontal stripes on anything moving. Until now Crisp spotted that and asked you to fix it in another app first, because an upscaler treats those stripes as detail worth sharpening. It now does the work for you, before anything else runs. Footage that started life on film gets special treatment: Crisp puts the original twenty-four frames a second back rather than blending them, so you get the frames that were actually shot, and the render finishes sooner because there is less to enhance.
